value.name: hdfs.url
value.documentation: The HDFS connection URL. This configuration has the format of hdfs://hostname:port and specifies the HDFS to export data to. This property is deprecated and will be removed in future releases. Use ``store.url`` instead.

value.name: hadoop.conf.dir
value.documentation: The Hadoop configuration directory.

value.name: hadoop.home
value.documentation: The Hadoop home directory.

value.name: logs.dir
value.documentation: Top level directory to store the write ahead logs.

value.name: hdfs.authentication.kerberos
value.documentation: Configuration indicating whether HDFS is using Kerberos for authentication.

value.name: connect.hdfs.principal
value.documentation: The principal to use when HDFS is using Kerberos to for authentication.

value.name: connect.hdfs.keytab
value.documentation: The path to the keytab file for the HDFS connector principal. This keytab file should only be readable by the connector user.

value.name: hdfs.namenode.principal
value.documentation: The principal for HDFS Namenode.

value.name: kerberos.ticket.renew.period.ms
value.documentation: The period in milliseconds to renew the Kerberos ticket.

value.name: max.retries
value.documentation: The maximum number of retry attempts for transient errors. If the number of attempts exceeds this value, the task will fail.

value.name: retry.on.kerberos.cred.errors
value.documentation: If true, the connector will retry on Kerberos credential errors such as GSSException.NO_CRED and GSSException.CREDENTIALS_EXPIRED. If false, these errors will not be retried.

value.name: flush.size
value.documentation: Number of records written to store before invoking file commits.

value.name: rotate.interval.ms
value.documentation: The time interval in milliseconds to invoke file commits. You can configure this parameter so that the time interval is determined by using a timestamp extractor (for example, Kafka Record Time, Record Field, or Wall Clock extractor). When the first record is processed, a timestamp is set as the base time. This is useful if you require exactly-once-semantics. This configuration ensures that file commits are invoked at every configured interval. The default value ``-1`` indicates that this feature is disabled.

value.name: rotate.schedule.interval.ms
value.documentation: The time interval in milliseconds to periodically invoke file commits. This configuration ensures that file commits are invoked at every configured interval. Time of commit will be adjusted to 00:00 of selected timezone. The commit will be performed at the scheduled time, regardless of the previous commit time or number of messages. This configuration is useful when you have to commit your data based on current server time, for example at the beginning of every hour. The default value ``-1`` means that this feature is disabled.

value.name: schemas.cache.config
value.documentation: The size of the schema cache used in the Avro converter.

value.name: enhanced.avro.schema.support
value.documentation: Enable enhanced avro schema support in AvroConverter: Enum symbol preservation and Package Name awareness

value.name: connect.meta.data
value.documentation: Allow connect converter to add its metadata to the output schema

value.name: retry.backoff.ms
value.documentation: The retry backoff in milliseconds. This config is used to notify Kafka connect to retry delivering a message batch or performing recovery in case of transient exceptions.

value.name: shutdown.timeout.ms
value.documentation: Clean shutdown timeout. This makes sure that asynchronous Hive metastore updates are completed during connector shutdown.

value.name: filename.offset.zero.pad.width
value.documentation: Width to zero pad offsets in store's filenames if offsets are too short in order to provide fixed width filenames that can be ordered by simple lexicographic sorting.

value.name: avro.codec
value.documentation: The Avro compression codec to be used for output  files. Available values: null, deflate, snappy and bzip2 (CodecSource is org.apache.avro.file.CodecFactory)

value.name: allow.optional.map.keys
value.documentation: Allow optional string map key when converting from Connect Schema to Avro Schema.

value.name: schema.compatibility
value.documentation: The schema compatibility rule to use when the connector is observing schema changes. The supported configurations are NONE, BACKWARD, FORWARD and FULL.

value.name: topics.dir
value.documentation: Top level directory to store the data ingested from Kafka.

value.name: store.url
value.documentation: Store's connection URL, if applicable.

value.name: directory.delim
value.documentation: Directory delimiter pattern

value.name: file.delim
value.documentation: File delimiter pattern

value.name: partitioner.class
value.documentation: The partitioner to use when writing data to the store. You can use ``DefaultPartitioner``, which preserves the Kafka partitions; ``FieldPartitioner``, which partitions the data to different directories according to the value of the partitioning field specified in ``partition.field.name``; ``TimeBasedPartitioner``, which partitions data according to ingestion time.

value.name: partition.field.name
value.documentation: The name of the partitioning field when FieldPartitioner is used.

value.name: partition.duration.ms
value.documentation: The duration of a partition milliseconds used by ``TimeBasedPartitioner``. The default value -1 means that we are not using ``TimeBasedPartitioner``.

value.name: path.format
value.documentation: This configuration is used to set the format of the data directories when partitioning with ``TimeBasedPartitioner``. The format set in this configuration converts the Unix timestamp to proper directories strings. For example, if you set ``path.format='year'=YYYY/'month'=MM/'day'=dd/'hour'=HH``, the data directories will have the format ``/year=2015/month=12/day=07/hour=15/``.

value.name: locale
value.documentation: The locale to use when partitioning with ``TimeBasedPartitioner``. Used to format dates and times. For example, use ``en-US`` for US English, ``en-GB`` for UK English, or ``fr-FR`` for French (in France). These may vary by Java version. See the `available locales <http://www.localeplanet.com/java/>`__.

value.name: timezone
value.documentation: The timezone to use when partitioning with ``TimeBasedPartitioner``. Used to format and compute dates and times. All timezone IDs must be specified in the long format, such as ``America/Los_Angeles``, ``America/New_York``, and ``Europe/Paris``, or ``UTC``. Alternatively a locale independent, fixed offset, datetime zone can be specified in form ``[+-]hh:mm``. Support for these timezones may vary by Java version. See the `available timezones within each locale <http://www.localeplanet.com/java/>`__, such as `those within the US English locale <http://www.localeplanet.com/java/en-US/index.html>`__.

value.name: timestamp.extractor
value.documentation: The extractor that gets the timestamp for records when partitioning with ``TimeBasedPartitioner``. It can be set to ``Wallclock``, ``Record`` or ``RecordField`` in order to use one of the built-in timestamp extractors or be given the fully-qualified class name of a user-defined class that extends the ``TimestampExtractor`` interface.

value.name: timestamp.field
value.documentation: The record field to be used as timestamp by the timestamp extractor.

value.name: hive.integration
value.documentation: Configuration indicating whether to integrate with Hive when running the connector.

value.name: hive.metastore.uris
value.documentation: The Hive metastore URIs, can be IP address or fully-qualified domain name and port of the metastore host.

value.name: hive.conf.dir
value.documentation: Hive configuration directory

value.name: hive.home
value.documentation: Hive home directory.

value.name: hive.database
value.documentation: The database to use when the connector creates tables in Hive.

value.name: storage.class
value.documentation: The underlying storage layer.

value.name: format.class
value.documentation: The format class to use when writing data to the store.

value.name: confluent.license
value.documentation: Confluent will issue a license key to each subscriber. The license key will be a short snippet of text that you can copy and paste. Without the license key, you can use the connector for a 30-day trial period. If you are a subscriber, please contact Confluent Support for more information.

value.name: confluent.topic.bootstrap.servers
value.documentation: A list of host/port pairs to use for establishing the initial connection to the Kafka cluster used for licensing. All servers in the cluster will be discovered from the initial connection. This list should be in the form ``host1:port1,host2:port2,...``. These servers are used only for the initial connection to discover the full cluster membership, which may change dynamically, so this list need not contain the full set of servers. You may want more than one, in case a server is down.

value.name: confluent.topic
value.documentation: Name of the Kafka topic used for Confluent Platform configuration, including licensing information.

value.name: confluent.topic.replication.factor
value.documentation: The replication factor for the Kafka topic used for Confluent Platform configuration, including licensing information. This is used only if the topic does not already exist, and the default of 3 is appropriate for production use. If you are using a development environment with less than 3 brokers, you must set this to the number of brokers (often 1).

value.name: name
value.documentation: Globally unique name to use for this connector.

value.name: connector.class
value.documentation: Name or alias of the class for this connector. Must be a subclass of org.apache.kafka.connect.connector.Connector. If the connector is org.apache.kafka.connect.file.FileStreamSinkConnector, you can either specify this full name,  or use "FileStreamSink" or "FileStreamSinkConnector" to make the configuration a bit shorter

value.name: tasks.max
value.documentation: Maximum number of tasks to use for this connector.

value.name: key.converter
value.documentation: Converter class used to convert between Kafka Connect format and the serialized form that is written to Kafka. This controls the format of the keys in messages written to or read from Kafka, and since this is independent of connectors it allows any connector to work with any serialization format. Examples of common formats include JSON and Avro.

value.name: value.converter
value.documentation: Converter class used to convert between Kafka Connect format and the serialized form that is written to Kafka. This controls the format of the values in messages written to or read from Kafka, and since this is independent of connectors it allows any connector to work with any serialization format. Examples of common formats include JSON and Avro.

value.name: header.converter
value.documentation: HeaderConverter class used to convert between Kafka Connect format and the serialized form that is written to Kafka. This controls the format of the header values in messages written to or read from Kafka, and since this is independent of connectors it allows any connector to work with any serialization format. Examples of common formats include JSON and Avro. By default, the SimpleHeaderConverter is used to serialize header values to strings and deserialize them by inferring the schemas.

value.name: transforms
value.documentation: Aliases for the transformations to be applied to records.

value.name: predicates
value.documentation: Aliases for the predicates used by transformations.

value.name: config.action.reload
value.documentation: The action that Connect should take on the connector when changes in external configuration providers result in a change in the connector's configuration properties. A value of 'none' indicates that Connect will do nothing. A value of 'restart' indicates that Connect should restart/reload the connector with the updated configuration properties.The restart may actually be scheduled in the future if the external configuration provider indicates that a configuration value will expire in the future.

value.name: errors.retry.timeout
value.documentation: The maximum duration in milliseconds that a failed operation will be reattempted. The default is 0, which means no retries will be attempted. Use -1 for infinite retries.

value.name: errors.retry.delay.max.ms
value.documentation: The maximum duration in milliseconds between consecutive retry attempts. Jitter will be added to the delay once this limit is reached to prevent thundering herd issues.
value.display_name: Maximum Delay Between Retries for Errors

value.name: errors.tolerance
value.documentation: Behavior for tolerating errors during connector operation. 'none' is the default value and signals that any error will result in an immediate connector task failure; 'all' changes the behavior to skip over problematic records.

value.name: errors.log.enable
value.documentation: If true, write each error and the details of the failed operation and problematic record to the Connect application log. This is 'false' by default, so that only errors that are not tolerated are reported.

value.name: errors.log.include.messages
value.documentation: Whether to include in the log the Connect record that resulted in a failure. For sink records, the topic, partition, offset, and timestamp will be logged. For source records, the key and value (and their schemas), all headers, and the timestamp, Kafka topic, Kafka partition, source partition, and source offset will be logged. This is 'false' by default, which will prevent record keys, values, and headers from being written to log files.

value.name: topics
value.documentation: List of topics to consume, separated by commas

value.name: topics.regex
value.documentation: Regular expression giving topics to consume. Under the hood, the regex is compiled to a java.util.regex.Pattern. Only one of topics or topics.regex should be specified.

value.name: errors.deadletterqueue.topic.name
value.documentation: The name of the topic to be used as the dead letter queue (DLQ) for messages that result in an error when processed by this sink connector, or its transformations or converters. The topic name is blank by default, which means that no messages are to be recorded in the DLQ.

value.name: errors.deadletterqueue.topic.replication.factor
value.documentation: Replication factor used to create the dead letter queue topic when it doesn't already exist.
value.display_name: Dead Letter Queue Topic Replication Factor

value.name: errors.deadletterqueue.context.headers.enable
value.documentation: If true, add headers containing error context to the messages written to the dead letter queue. To avoid clashing with headers from the original record, all error context header keys, all error context header keys will start with __connect.errors.
